claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances.

Let me start with: **Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 8 years old and I wanted to check if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

**Are you responsible for Alex? By this I mean, does he live with you, and do you look after him and contribute to the costs of raising him (such as food, clothing, and other expenses)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, Alex does normally live with me, yes. But I should mention that he's actually been in local authority care for a few months now. He doesn't come home to stay with me - he's there full-time at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for sharing that important information. This is relevant to your eligibility.

**Just to clarify - while Alex is in local authority care, are you still contributing to any of the costs of raising him, or is the local authority covering all his care and living expenses?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not contributing anything at the moment. The local authority is covering all his expenses while he's in their care.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I have one more important question:

**Is the local authority paying you any money to look after Alex (such as fostering payments or similar), or are they responsible for him without any payments to you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, they're not paying me anything. The local authority is just responsible for him while he's in care - I'm not receiving any fostering payments or anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've told me, unfortunately you would not be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex while he remains in local authority care. Here's why:

To qualify for Child Benefit, you must be responsible for the child - meaning they must live with you and you must be contributing to the costs of raising them. Since Alex is currently in local authority care full-time and the local authority is covering all his expenses (and you're not contributing to his costs), you don't meet the responsibility requirement during this period.

**However**, if Alex returns to live with you in the future and you resume responsibility for his care and costs, you would be able to claim Child Benefit for him at that time.
